> **Overtourism**
> 
> For decades, cities competed to attract as many visitors as possible. Tourism brought money, jobs and international attention, and few local governments questioned whether there could be too much of it. That attitude has changed sharply in the last ten years.
> 
> Several European cities now receive more overnight visitors each year than they have residents. In Venice, the permanent population has fallen below 50,000, while roughly 20 million people visit annually. Local shops selling everyday goods have been replaced by souvenir stalls, and rents have risen far beyond what ordinary families can afford. Residents argue that the city is becoming a museum rather than a place to live.
> 
> Responses have varied. Some cities have introduced entry fees for day visitors; others have limited the number of new hotel licences or banned short-term holiday rentals in the centre. Critics say such measures simply push tourists into neighbouring areas without reducing the overall numbers. What is clear is that the assumption that more tourists are always better no longer goes unchallenged.

6. Venice has fewer than 50,000 permanent residents.
7. Entry fees have successfully reduced total visitor numbers.
8. All European cities have introduced restrictions on tourism.

writing.de_tom_tat: Viết 80–90 từ về quy định ở khách sạn/nơi làm việc: 2 điều bắt buộc, 1 bị cấm, 1 không cần thiết.
writing.bai_mau: There are a few rules in my office. You must wear your ID card at all times, and you must log out of your computer before leaving. You mustn't bring food into the server room — that is strictly forbidden. However, you don't have to wear formal clothes; jeans are perfectly acceptable. You don't need to ask permission for short breaks either, as long as you finish your work on time.

cham_diem.tieu_chi: must / mustn't / don't have to đúng (3đ)
cham_diem.vi_sao: must wear, must log out (bắt buộc) · mustn't bring (bị cấm) · don't have to wear, don't need to ask (không cần thiết). Phân biệt đúng cả ba mức.
2 bắt buộc · 1 cấm · 2 không cần thiết.
"strictly forbidden", "perfectly acceptable", "as long as" — cụm từ đúng ngữ cảnh quy định.

dang_hoc: Ba mức khác nhau, đừng lẫn: mustn't = bị cấm · don't have to = không cần nhưng được phép · must = bắt buộc.
Đây là điểm sai kinh điển: "You mustn't wear a tie" nghĩa là CẤM đeo cà vạt, không phải "không cần đeo".
as long as = miễn là — cụm rất hay dùng khi nói về điều kiện.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ You mustn't wear formal clothes (ý: không cần) → ✅ You don't have to wear formal clothes
❌ You must to wear an ID card → ✅ You must wear an ID card
❌ You haven't to ask → ✅ You don't have to ask

speaking.de_tom_tat: Describe the rules at your workplace. / Are there rules you disagree with? / What makes a good hotel?

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Describe the rules at your workplace.
cau_tra_loi.mau: They're fairly relaxed. We must wear ID cards and log out of our computers, but we don't have to follow a dress code. Jeans are fine.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: So sánh cái bắt buộc với cái không cần trong cùng câu — thể hiện bạn phân biệt được must và don't have to.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Are there rules you disagree with?
cau_tra_loi.mau: One, actually. We're not allowed to work from home more than twice a week, which doesn't make much sense for my role since most of my work is online.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "We're not allowed to" là cách nói khác của mustn't, tự nhiên hơn khi kể về quy định.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Cleanliness above all, then a quiet room. Staff who actually solve problems matter more than a fancy lobby. And decent wifi is essential these days.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Xếp thứ tự ưu tiên (above all, then, matter more than) — cấu trúc lập luận đơn giản mà hiệu quả.

cham_diem.vi_sao: must wear · don't have to follow · not allowed to work.
mustn't /ˈmʌsnt/ — chữ t đầu tiên CÂM, chỉ đọc một /t/.

meo_noi: mustn't đọc /ˈmʌsnt/ — bỏ hẳn âm /t/ ở giữa.
"be allowed to" là cách nói lịch sự hơn khi kể quy định của người khác.
